answer: Agents can earn transaction weight only after completing a sequence of small tasks whose outputs are checked against randomly assigned peers, with rewards locked until later rounds. A single operator may create many identities, but each must pay the same upfront stake and sustain distinct, consistent work; copied outputs expose coordination and can forfeit the stake. The oasis, terrace, and tundra are simply task settings, not identity credentials, so names alone buy no influence. The attacker pays capital and ongoing labor for every credible identity.
